description: Somos PENTANET, un equipo multidisciplinario enfocado en Sistemas y Ciencias de la Tierra que optamos por el desafío de Armonización de Puntos Calientes de MODIS y VIIRS
summary:
NaSAT Space is a GIS and Remote Sensing-based platform that integrates 26 years of NASA satellite data from MODIS and VIIRS sensors. We developed a system capable of processing 2.4 million raw data records and implementing an Early Warning System that estimates the probability of wildfire occurrence.
NaSAT Space generates a hexagonal grid with cells covering 36 km², reducing false positives caused by industrial activities and reflective surfaces through seasonal statistical calibration.
Additionally, the platform provides statistical reports and wildfire probability forecasts at regional, local, and user-defined spatial scales, improving wildfire monitoring, decision-making, and emergency response across the territory.
details:
Project Overview

NaSAT is a Wildfire Early Warning System that collects data from MODIS and VIIRS sensors to estimate the number of potential wildfire events and their probability of occurrence using Poisson-based statistical analysis. This allows users to visualise wildfire occurrence probabilities for the following months through an interactive map and access reports that help authorities make better-informed decisions.

Technology and Development

This GIS and Remote Sensing-based platform was developed using TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python, with Google Cloud for deployment, Docker for containerisation, and GoDaddy for domain management.

The analysis combines Poisson-based statistical modelling with the professional judgement and geographical expertise of a Geographical Engineer, ensuring a more meaningful interpretation of wildfire patterns and risks.

Innovation and Benefits

NaSAT provides an intuitive way to analyse complex satellite data with just a few clicks. Users can access forecasts, interactive visualisations, graphs, and statistical reports without requiring specialised technical knowledge.

Team and Project Impact

As the PENTANET Team, we started by harmonising historical data from MODIS and VIIRS, turning different satellite observations into a consistent source of information. We took this a step further by developing a service with public-interest value, estimating how many wildfire events may occur in the future and the probability of their occurrence, supporting proactive planning and better-informed decisions.
